correctness.rationale: The delivered narrowing claims precisely the labelled basin sizes, period-resolved entry table, and attained entry cutoffs for P(5) and P(9) at half degree. Independently built both graphs from finite-field squares, generated every successor, removed zero-indegree states to find the recurrent cycles, and assigned transient distances by reverse breadth-first search. This checked all 243 and 19683 assignments and reproduced every cell, all individual cycle basins, and both maxima. The second independent finite reconstruction also agrees. The proof in the repair correctly explains the zero transient basin sizes at P(9): in a Latin-square target, target colors 1 and 2 force their predecessor colors, and two known predecessor excitations forbid every target-0 vertex from previously resting. The original larger-order extinction statement was also checked and is mathematically correct: a firing on a periodic orbit uses at least θ incoming contacts, each edge gives at most the smaller of its endpoint firing counts, and half-degree forces equality, yielding A u_t=θ(u_(t−1)+u_(t+1)); temporal Fourier modes require algebraic-integer eigenvalue ratios. For q≥13 the normalized nonsquare eigenvalues have nonintegral quadratic trace and the square-order ratios are nonintegral rational numbers. The repair credits that all-order exclusion as covered and does not infer it from enumeration.
residual_risks: Finite labelled counts only, at the exact half-degree threshold. No assumption about unseen behavior on larger graphs, and no proof by sampled configurations.

value.rationale: These graphs are selected by a natural extremal boundary: they are the only Paley orders allowing nonzero waves at critical contact. The finite finding compares attraction rather than merely existence: each pentagon wave attracts 40 transient states, while every grid wave is isolated despite the larger number of recurrent configurations. Per-cycle sizes and exact entry profiles quantify an observable distinction and provide sharp reproducible finite benchmarks; the already-implied global dichotomy is not counted as new value.
residual_risks: No claim of a general theory of basin sizes or a useful wider-order transient bound.
